author: Al Jazeera English
description:
A SpaceX capsule transporting four astronauts from the International Space Station (ISS) has splashed down in the Pacific Ocean after completing the first-ever medical evacuation in the orbital lab’s history, video footage from NASA has shown.
The SpaceX Dragon spacecraft, known as the “Endeavour”, began its 10-and-a-half-hour descent from orbit at 22:30 GMT on Wednesday and landed off the coast of San Diego, California, at 12:41am local time (08:41 GMT) on Thursday.
The video feed from NASA showed the landing of the capsule carrying American astronauts Mike Fincke and Zena Cardman, Russian cosmonaut Oleg Platonov and Japanese astronaut Kimiya Yui.
It's the first time in the station's history a mission has been cut short for medical reasons.
NASA hasn't revealed which crew member is ill but says they are in good spirits and undergoing thorough checks in hospital.

Al Jazeera’s Caley Callahan reports.
Robert Massey is the Deputy Executive Director at the Royal Astronomical Society. He

Iranian airspace is once again open to traffic, after it was shut for several hours.
All flights into and out of the country were grounded, except some arrivals that had been given prior permission.
International flights that would normally fly over Iran had to divert.
Iranian airspace has now reopened but several carriers say they're avoiding it until further notice. Airlines have told passengers to expect delays.

Internet network tracker NetBlocks says the internet blackout in Iran has now lasted more than 6 days. 
Elon Musk’s Starlink is reportedly offering free service to some users in the country - one of the few ways images and videos of the protests have made their way out of Iran. 

Al Jazeera's Tohid Asadi has the latest in Tehran, Iran.

description:
The US capture of Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro has raised questions about who will be next to lead the country.
Maduro's second-in-command is currently interim president, and prominent opposition figure Maria Corina Machado will meet Donald Trump in the White House on Thursday
But many within the country say they're more focused on their day-to-day realities than politics.

Al Jazeera’s Noris Soto reports from the capital, Caracas.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
There's been another crane collapse in Thailand less than 24 hours after a similar incident in the country killed dozens of people.
This one happened in Samut Sakhon, a coastal area on the outskirts of Bangkok.
Local reports suggest several vehicles were crushed when the crane toppled down.
At least one person is confirmed to have been killed.
Emergency services are on the scene, helping those affected.

Meanwhile, Thailand's Prime Minister has ordered an investigation into Wednesday's construction crane crash.
At least 32 people on board a passenger train died when a crane collapsed onto it in Sikhio and at least 64 other people were injured.
The crane was working on a high-speed rail project linking southeast Asia and China. 

Al Jazeera’s Tony Cheng reports from the scene of the accident in Sikhio District, Thailand.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Denmark says fundamental disagreements remain with the US over the future of Greenland. President Donald Trump has said he wants to take over the territory 'one way or another', arguing anything short of full American control is unacceptable. But, during a meeting with Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio, the foreign ministers of Denmark and Greenland said they made it clear they were willing to cooperate on security without relinquishing ownership.

Al Jazeera’s Chief US Correspondent Alan Fisher reports from Washington.
